item.title: ZBloggers Monitor · Monday 27 July 2026 — Ukrainian drones kill five in Rostov; Iranian ship hit in Caspian
item.description:

Pro-Kremlin channels led with deadly Ukrainian drone strikes across Russian regions—five killed in Rostov and casualties in Belgorod, Kerch, and LPR—while a claimed Ukrainian attack on an Iranian vessel in the Caspian dominated the geopolitical framing. Sentiment split sharply: grievance over strikes on Russia against upbeat claims of frontline gains and Putin's troop-strength increase.

🚩 Russia internal sentiment jumps +69. Domestic coverage turned sharply positive, driven by Putin's authorized 25,000-troop increase to 2.43 million, a new migrant-control law, and showcases of upgraded BMP-3s, combat robots and air-defense production.

🚩 Mobilisation rumours across three channels. WarGonzo, Poddubny and Sladkov all posted on force expansion—a 25,000-personnel increase to 2.426 million effective August 1, plus Sladkov's claim of 50,000 added in two months—framed positively as voluntary growth.

🚩 No criticism of Putin. The watchlisted 'Criticism of Putin' theme was absent; the day's two criticism posts targeted Ukrainian figures, and Putin coverage was uniformly laudatory.

  1. Ukrainian drone strikes kill five in Rostov, wound dozens (✓ multiple channels)
    Multiple channels reported a Ukrainian drone attack on Rostov-on-Don killing five (with reports of children among the dead) and thirteen wounded in Belgorod including two children; further strikes reported on Kerch (ten injured) and LPR (two killed). Casualty figures are channel-sourced and unconfirmed. source ↗
  2. Claimed Ukrainian strike on Iranian ship in Caspian Sea (✓ multiple channels)
    Channels amplified claims that Ukraine attacked an Iranian vessel in the Caspian Sea, killing a sailor, with Iran reportedly threatening retaliation—one channel citing a 'World War III' response. Framed as escalating regional tensions among Caspian states; claim is unconfirmed. source ↗

    Channels reported Putin authorized a 25,000-personnel increase to a total 2.426 million, effective August 1, framed positively; Sladkov separately claimed forces grew by 50,000 in two months. Flagged as mobilisation-related rhetoric across three channels. source ↗
  4. Claimed capture of Kommunarovka on Dnipropetrovsk direction (✓ multiple channels)
